```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)

library(fivethirtyeight)

candy <- fivethirtyeight::candy_rankings

candy <- candy |>
  mutate(type = case_when(
    chocolate & fruity ~ "both",
    chocolate ~ "chocolate",
    fruity ~ "fruity",
    .default = "other"
  ))

##count(candy, type)
```

## Row 1

```{r}
#| content: valuebox

###list(
 ### icon = "basket",
  ###color = "warning",

```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Number of Fruity Candies"

###list(
  ###icon = "life-preserver",
 ### color = "red",
 ### value = sum(candy$type == "fruity"))

```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Most sugary"

highest_sugar <- candy |>
  slice_max(sugarpercent, n = 1)

list(
  icon = "boxes",
  color = "pink",
  value = paste(highest_sugar$competitorname,
                highest_sugar$sugarpercent))##
```

## Row 1

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Least Sugary"


lowest_sugar <- candy |>
  slice_min(sugarpercent, n = 1)

list(
  icon = "boxes",
  color = "blue",
  value = paste(lowest_sugar$competitorname,
                lowest_sugar$sugarpercent))
```

## Row 2

```{r}
#Sugar Rush. Does more sugar mean more popular? Make a scatter with a trend line, plus value boxes for the most and least sugary candies.


sugar_popular <- ggplot(candy, aes(sugarpercent, winpercent, color = "pink"))+
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "lightblue")

ggplotly(sugar_popular)
```
